knowledge:
- key_parameters: obj=SummarizedExperiment object containing expression and survival data ;; bfname=Base name for automatically generated output files ;; n_iter=Number of iterations for the random permutation test in km_opt_pcut ;; wlabels=Logical indicating whether to write low/high sample labels to a CSV file ;; wpdf=Logical indicating whether to write Kaplan-Meier plots to a PDF file ;; verbose=Logical indicating whether to print progress messages ;; nproc=Number of processors to use for parallel execution in km_opt_pcut ;; quant=Quantile (0 to 100) used for stratification in km_qcut ;; cutoff=User-supplied fixed value used for stratification in km_ucut ;; min_uval=Minimum percentage of unique values required for a feature to be analyzed
- alternatives: km_opt_scut is a fast exploratory alternative to km_opt_pcut that does not use the permutation test to estimate statistical significance. km_qcut and km_ucut are non-optimization alternatives that perform a single log-rank test per feature using quantile or fixed thresholds.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have right-censored survival data and quantitative features (such as RNA-seq, microarray, or ssGSEA signatures) for a cohort of subjects, and you want to find or validate prognostic thresholds.
- pitfalls: The permutation test in km_opt_pcut is highly computationally intensive; it is recommended to first filter features using km_opt_scut before running km_opt_pcut. The p-value from km_opt_scut is for informational purposes only and does not correct for multiple testing during optimization. Sample identifiers in the survival and expression files must match exactly.

workflows.name: optimal_cutoff_permutation
workflows.intent: Identify optimal prognostic cutoffs for features and estimate their statistical significance using a permutation test.
input: survival_data.txt (tab-delimited file with sample_id, stime, and scens columns)
example_genes.txt (tab-delimited file with features in rows and samples in columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Create a SummarizedExperiment object from the input files ;; 2. Run the permutation test and cutoff optimization
workflows.code:
fdat = system.file("extdata", "example_genes.txt", package = "kmcut")
sdat = system.file("extdata", "survival_data.txt", package = "kmcut")
se = create_se_object(efile = fdat, sfile = sdat)
km_opt_pcut(obj = se, bfname = "test", n_iter = 10, wlabels = TRUE, wpdf = FALSE, verbose = FALSE, nproc = 1)

workflows.name: optimal_cutoff_exploratory
workflows.intent: Perform a fast exploratory search for optimal prognostic cutoffs without running the time-consuming permutation test.
input: survival_data.txt (tab-delimited file with sample_id, stime, and scens columns)
example_genes.txt (tab-delimited file with features in rows and samples in columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Create a SummarizedExperiment object from the input files ;; 2. Search for optimal cutoffs
workflows.code:
fdat = system.file("extdata", "example_genes.txt", package = "kmcut")
sdat = system.file("extdata", "survival_data.txt", package = "kmcut")
se <- create_se_object(efile = fdat, sfile = sdat)
km_opt_scut(obj = se, bfname = "test", wpdf = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)

workflows.name: fixed_or_quantile_cutoff
workflows.intent: Stratify samples and calculate log-rank test p-values using a specified quantile or a fixed user-supplied cutoff value.
input: survival_data.txt (tab-delimited file with sample_id, stime, and scens columns)
example_genes.txt (tab-delimited file with features in rows and samples in columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Create a SummarizedExperiment object from the input files ;; 2. Stratify samples using a quantile cutoff or a fixed user-defined cutoff
workflows.code:
fdat = system.file("extdata", "example_genes.txt", package = "kmcut")
sdat = system.file("extdata", "survival_data.txt", package="kmcut")
se <- create_se_object(efile = fdat, sfile = sdat)
km_qcut(obj = se, bfname = "test", quant = 50, wpdf = FALSE)
km_ucut(obj = se, bfname = "test", cutoff = 5, min_uval = 90, wpdf = FALSE)

workflows.name: cutoff_validation
workflows.intent: Validate previously determined stratification cutoffs on an independent validation dataset.
workflows.stages: 1. Create SummarizedExperiment for training data ;; 2. Run training stratification to generate a cutoff file ;; 3. Create SummarizedExperiment for validation data ;; 4. Validate the training cutoffs on the validation data
workflows.code:
fdat1 <- system.file("extdata", "expression_data_1.txt", package = "kmcut")
fdat2 <- system.file("extdata", "expression_data_2.txt", package = "kmcut")
sdat <- system.file("extdata", "survival_data.txt", package = "kmcut")
se1 <- create_se_object(efile = fdat1, sfile = sdat)
km_qcut(obj = se1, bfname = "training_data", quant = 50, min_uval = 40)
se2 <- create_se_object(efile = fdat2, sfile = sdat)
km_val_cut(infile = "training_data_KM_quant_50.txt", obj = se2, bfname = "test", wpdf = TRUE, min_uval = 40)

workflows.name: batch_cox_regression
workflows.intent: Fit univariate Cox proportional hazard regression models and perform likelihood ratio tests for all features in batch.
input: survival_data.txt (tab-delimited file with sample_id, stime, and scens columns)
example_genes.txt (tab-delimited file with features in rows and samples in columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Create a SummarizedExperiment object from the input files ;; 2. Perform batch Cox regression
workflows.code:
fdat = system.file("extdata", "example_genes.txt", package = "kmcut")
sdat = system.file("extdata", "survival_data.txt", package = "kmcut")
se <- create_se_object(efile = fdat, sfile = sdat)
ucox_batch(obj = se, bfname = "test")

workflows.name: cox_risk_prediction
workflows.intent: Fit univariate Cox proportional hazard models on training data and calculate risk scores for a test dataset.
workflows.stages: 1. Create SummarizedExperiment for training data ;; 2. Create SummarizedExperiment for test data ;; 3. Fit Cox models on training data and calculate risk scores for test data
workflows.code:
fdat1 = system.file("extdata", "expression_data_1.txt", package = "kmcut")
fdat2 = system.file("extdata", "expression_data_2.txt", package = "kmcut")
sdat = system.file("extdata", "survival_data.txt", package = "kmcut")
se1 <- create_se_object(efile = fdat1, sfile = sdat)
se2 <- create_se_object(efile = fdat2, sfile = sdat)
ucox_pred(obj1 = se1, obj2 = se2, bfname = "demo", min_uval = 40)
